subject: Dedicated capacity recap — OrbitCare next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@orbitcare.ai>, Erica Lopez <erica.lopez@orbitcare.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap — OrbitCare next steps

Hi Samir / Erica —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same page: 

Key pain points you described:
- Latency spikes on peak clinical hours causing degraded UX for clinician workflows (95th pct token latency > 2.5s).
- Unpredictable token spend on hosted endpoints; need predictable unit economics for budgeting.
- Need data isolation and auditability for PHI workflows (VPC + audit logs + KMS).

Goals from this engagement:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) to guarantee latency and throughput for core inference paths.
- Private deployment options for PHI-handling endpoints with customer-managed VPC and KMS.
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime on dedicated routes, 95th pct token latency < 1.2s for short prompts.
- Phased scaling: pilot -> spike protection -> full production rollout over 8-12 weeks.

Proposed Redwood Dedicated plan (high level):
- Reserved baseline: 4 x A100/P4d-equivalent GPUs dedicated to OrbitCare (single-tenant pool).
- Burst capacity: automatic access to +2 GPUs for traffic spikes (policy-based, billed as burst).
- Isolation: private VPC peering, per-route audit logs, KMS integration for model payloads.
- Autoscaling policy: scale-in/out thresholds tuned for median sequence lengths and 99th pct latency.
- Cost profile: baseline reserved monthly fee + per-token inference units during burst/overage. Detailed breakdown attached.

Next steps (action items):
1) I attached the updated proposal and SOW (redwood_dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf; sow_orbitcare_draft.docx). Please review and share with legal/procurement.
2) Dev/infra call with Dev Patel to validate VPC and KMS details — can we schedule next Tue/Mar 2?
3) Procurement questions: contract term, invoicing cadence — Erica / procurement, can you confirm preferred term (12 vs 24 months) and PO process?
4) We'll provide SOC2 evidence and a short security packet for your compliance team.

If I've missed anything, flag it here and I'll update. Appreciate the time — excited to get OrbitCare onto dedicated capacity.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf, sow_orbitcare_draft.docx

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap — OrbitCare next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) Can you include a one-page SOC2 / security summary and an example audit log export format in the packet for our compliance reviewer?
2) For the burst capacity, what's the lead time to spin additional GPUs outside the reserved pool? Are bursts instantaneous or do they require a warm-up window?
3) On pricing: can you give a split between reserved monthly commitment vs per-token burst charges so I can model FY26 budget?

We prefer a 12-month term to start, but if there's a strong discount for 24 months, happy to discuss. Also keen to get Dev Patel on a technical call — Tue/Mar 2 at 10am PT works for our infra folks if that works for you.

—Samir
Head of AI Engineering | OrbitCare

Thanks all — attaching the SOW draft and updated proposal per Samir's requests. High-level clarifications inline below and in the attachments: 

- SOC2/security packet: attached one-pager + link to full compliance folder. We'll also provide an example audit log export (CSV) for your reviewer.
- Burst capacity: typically warm pool activation is near-instant for our reserved customers (under 60s for compatible workloads). We'll include a note on sequence-length-related warm up in the tech appendix.
- Pricing split: attached breakout table (monthly reserved fee vs per-token burst/overage). For 12-month term the numbers in the proposal are standard; we can offer a 12% discount for a 24-month commit — happy to talk numbers with Vivek if you want a formal discount approval.
- Termination: standard pro-rata refund for unused committed months beyond a 60-day notice; details in MSA.
- Insurance/indemnity/data residency: included in MSA (US-hosted by default; can add EU residency clause for EU regions).

Action items: 
- Marissa: schedule Dev/infra call with Dev Patel — Tue, Mar 2 at 10:00 AM PT (confirmed).
- OrbitCare procurement: review attached MSA + SOW and send preferred markups by Mar 12.
- Redwood legal/finance: Viv ek, Laura, please review the requested termination/insurance points and confirm if the standard MSA covers OrbitCare's needs.

I'll follow up after the Dev call with a short tech notes doc and SOC2 export sample.

Best,
Marissa
